m2-refinement-precedence.title: weekend_state refinement/override precedence rule, TDD
m2-refinement-precedence.imperative: Add failing tests first proving the precedence rule (RED where the current implementation would get it wrong -- e.g. a naive unconditional override): (1) car_basis_posterior has axis X resolved with value V1; weekend_state (as_of_session='Q') has axis X status 'unresolved' -- after composing, weekend_relative_basis[X] must still be V1 (car_basis survives, NOT clobbered by the unresolved weekend_state axis); (2) car_basis_posterior has axis X resolved V1, weekend_state has axis X status 'resolved' with a DIFFERENT value V2 -- after composing, weekend_relative_basis[X] must be V2 (weekend_state, the more-refined signal, overrides when it has a real resolved answer), and axis_sigma[X] must be weekend_state's own sigma too. Implement: after seeding from car_basis_posterior (m1), if the weekend_state DataFrame (from the same load_as_of call) has any row at-or-before the cutoff, take its most-recent-present row (mirrors the primary-source picking rule) and, for each axis where THAT row's own axis_status[axis] == 'resolved', overwrite weekend_relative_basis[axis]/axis_sigma[axis] with the weekend_state row's value+sigma for that axis; an unresolved weekend_state axis must never touch weekend_relative_basis. Document this precedence rule explicitly in the module docstring (a real design decision, not incidental), including that today only as_of_session=='Q' can trigger it since build_weekend_state.py's model only processes Q rows.

preconditions.statement: m1 primary-source composer exists and its tests pass

postconditions.statement: TDD red: precedence tests written and observed failing against a naive/absent override implementation -- manual attest

m5-e2e-real-composed-data.title: End-to-end: re-verify append-only + as-of leakage on REAL G2/G3-composed data
m5-e2e-real-composed-data.imperative: Write tests/unit/physics/feature_view/test_e2e_integration.py: build a small synthetic WeekendStateModel (mirror test_build_weekend_state.py's make_frame/holdout.split/fit/transform convention) for one (year, gp_name, constructor) key, run it through the REAL build_weekend_state_records (G2) to get a Q-session WeekendStateRecord, and write it via FeatureViewStore.insert_weekend_state. Separately build a synthetic EstimateStore seeded with EstimateRecords (mirror test_build_car_basis.py's make_estimate_record convention) for the SAME (year, gp_name, constructor) across FP1/FP2/FP3/Q, each session carrying a DISTINCT sentinel value on one axis (e.g. drag_area_closed_m2 = 101/102/103/104 for FP1/FP2/FP3/Q), run it through the REAL build_car_basis_posterior_records (G3), and write the resulting CarBasisPosteriorRecords via FeatureViewStore.insert_car_basis_posterior. Then, via THIS gate's build_feature_view_row: (a) AS-OF LEAKAGE -- build+write the row at as_of_session='FP1' and assert weekend_relative_basis[sentinel_axis] == the FP1 sentinel only (never FP2/FP3/Q's sentinel values), and build+write at as_of_session='FP3' and assert it traces to the FP3 sentinel (never Q's); (b) APPEND-ONLY -- build+write at as_of_session='FP1' with model_version=1, then again with model_version=2 (a genuine version bump), and via read_feature_view confirm the model_version=1 row's fields are byte-identical to what was originally composed (not mutated by the v2 write); then attempt a THIRD build+write at as_of_session='FP1' with model_version=1 again (identical natural key) and assert it raises sqlite3.IntegrityError -- proving append-only holds through the REAL composer path end-to-end, not just G1's synthetic fixtures. This is an integration proof over already-built composers (m1-m3), not new production logic -- collapse TDD to the single green postcondition.
